text:
samir: Heads-up — 2 customer reports of p99 spikes (~5-10s) on eu-west dedicated clusters starting after last night's maintenance. Patterns: realtime small-batch workloads. Customers see auth retries and occasional 502s. Rolling spike across several hosts, not single-instance.

alyssa: Saw same in telemetry — p95 up ~30%, p99 dialed to 5-8s for embed/chat endpoints. Correlation: kernel + CUDA driver update rolled at 02:15 UTC.

dmitri: Repro from one affected node: intermittent NVMe tail latency + kvcache evictions. Grabbed dmesg + nvme stats. Snippet: 
```
[  123.456789] nvme nvme0q1: completion timeout
nvme0 0000:3b:00.0: I/O 0 qid 0 timeout, aborting
nvme0: I/O 3 QID 2 timeout, abort path
```
and 
```
# iostat -x 1 3
Device:         rrqm/s wrqm/s  r/s  w/s  rkB/s  wkB/s  avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1       0.00   0.00  5.00  0.10  4096.00  12.00  820.00    12.34  230.56  220.10 240.00  0.90  90.00
```

ops-bot: Deploybot: rollout(cuda-driver/v15.1.2)->eu-west completed 2026-03-16T02:16:08Z. No automatic rollback triggered.

maria: Also seeing a sharp increase in auth refresh retries from the same hosts — tokens were being retried ~3x before success, which amplifies tail. Looks like short bursts where KV cache misses cause model loads -> heavier disk IO -> token refresh timeouts.

kevin: Quick mitigation proposals: 
- route traffic away from eu-west pool to eu-central for affected customers (manual routing)
- reduce batching and max_concurrency on dedicated pool (to lower IO pressure)
- temporarily pin to smaller model variant for high-traffic routes
- escalate to vendor to look at nvme firmware + driver combo

samir: Can we triage non-invasively first? Steps I'm planning: collect full `nvme-cli` health + SMART, system journal around time windows, and KV cache eviction logs. Also want to test a single host rollback to previous CUDA driver to see if p99 drops.

dmitri: I ran a quick rollback on host eu-w-03 (safe canary): rolled driver back to v15.0.7, restarted runtime. Observed p99 drop from ~6.8s -> ~420ms for that host's traffic. Early signal indicates driver interaction.

alyssa: Nice repro. Still need to confirm whether GPU firmware or kernel preempt changes are compounding. Can we capture `dmesg | grep -i firmware` and `journalctl -u kubelet` for the window?

support-bot: Customer: "Our app saw latency spikes and 502 errors between 02:20-03:10 UTC. We retried and observed higher billing due to extra tokens." Customer asked for ETA and mitigation.

maria: For customer-facing mitigation — propose: 1) move their traffic to eu-central (we can do a host-level reroute), 2) offer to pin to older driver variant on Dedicated for their fleet, 3) credit for retry costs if they ask.

kevin: Operational steps I'm executing now: throttling batch size in eu-west realtime pool, bumping max qdepth per NVMe to reduce queue backlog, and scheduling a pause on further CUDA driver rollouts until we confirm root cause. Patching router to failover to eu-central when p99 > 2s for 5min.

dmitri: Repro checklist saved in thread: 
```
1) capture nvme-cli list and smart-log before/after spike
2) collect `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,utilization.gpu --format=csv -l 1` for 60s
3) dump runtime logs for kvcache eviction events (/var/log/redwood/kvcache.log)
4) run simple load test hitting small-batch embed route with and w/o driver rollback
```

samir: Can infra-sre schedule vendor escalation? If rollback confirms, we need vendor root-cause so future driver builds avoid regression. Include firmware versions and kernel configs in the ticket.

ops-bot: Pager: oncall@infra-pager notified. Incident P1 created (INC-2026-0453).

alyssa: Note: Authorization library shows increased latency on token refresh path when upstream calls to auth provider timed out (100ms -> 1.2s) during NVMe backlog windows. That links storage IO to auth retries (cascading).

kevin: Short term runbook (apply now): 
- fail traffic to eu-central for affected customers (in 5-10m)
- reduce model cache eviction threshold to keep hot models resident longer
- temporarily limit concurrent model loads per GPU to 2
- revert driver on 3/6 canary hosts then monitor p99 delta

maria: I'll draft customer comms summarizing mitigations and offer remediation credits. Keep wording: "post-maintenance driver interaction caused backend storage contention; we've routed your traffic and applied mitigations; root-cause investigation ongoing."

dmitri: After rollback on eu-w-03, I captured `perf top` and time-series of disk latency. Uploading artifacts to the incident ticket. Early vendor request: nvme vendor suggests trying firmware 2.11.4 on affected devices; will take maintenance window.

samir: OK — action owners: kevin (mitigations & routing), dmitri (rollback canaries & telemetry), maria (customer comms), alyssa (postmortem + perf diffs), samir (vendor escalation). We'll hold off on global rollback until vendor confirms. Keep this thread for updates. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Update: reroute applied for customer A at 03:05 UTC. Telemetry shows p99 for them back to baseline ~300ms.

support-bot: Customer A replied: "Thanks — latency reduced, appreciate the quick action. Please keep us posted on credits."

kevin: Monitoring: eu-west p99 trending down after throttles and canary rollbacks, but occasional spikes persist. Next step: schedule firmware upgrade during low traffic window and retest.

alyssa: Will prepare a short postmortem draft and include recommended rollback/validation gates for future CUDA/driver rollouts (canary size, storage qdepth probing, KV cache smoke tests).

samir: Closing note: this looks like an interaction between new CUDA driver behavior and NVMe IO scheduling under our KV cache load pattern that amplifies auth retries. Root cause not fully confirmed until vendor firmware test. Will update incident ticket with RCA when available.
